title: Spurious Attention Heads in Vision Transformers: Mechanistic Identification of Annotation-Driven Bias in Medical Chest X-Ray Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2610.21638v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision Transformers deployed in medical imaging exploit spurious correlations, yet the internal mechanisms remain unidentified and impossible to fix. We apply mechanistic interpretability to locate one such mechanism in ViT-Base 16: a single attention head (L8H10) that functions as a dedicated annotation-reader on chest X-rays, attending to corner text rather than lung pathology in 62% of 200 COVID-19 images. Causal validation via inpainting confirms annotation content rather than luminance or edge density drives the behaviour, increasing lung attention 1.52 times upon removal in affected images ($p{<}0.0001$). The finding replicates across NIH ChestX-ray14 (79%), DeiT-Base (88%), and ViT-Large 16 (80%), establishing spurious annotation-attending heads as a consistent property of ViT-family architectures across two datasets and three architectures. Full fine-tuning does not suppress the behaviour and may entrench it: 98.4% of spurious

translated_title: 视觉Transformer中的虚假注意力头：医学胸部X光分析中标注驱动偏差的机制性识别
translated_abstract: 部署于医学影像领域的视觉Transformer会利用虚假相关性，但其内部机制尚未被识别，因而无法修复。我们运用机制可解释性方法，在ViT-Base/16中定位到了这样一个机制：一个单独的注意力头（L8H10），它在胸部X光片上充当专门的“标注读取器”，在200张COVID-19图像中的62%里关注角落文字而非肺部病理。通过图像修复进行的因果验证证实，驱动该行为的是标注内容本身，而非亮度或边缘密度；在受影响图像中移除标注后，模型对肺部的注意力提升了1.52倍（p<0.0001）。该发现在NIH ChestX-ray14数据集（79%）、DeiT-Base架构（88%）以及ViT-Large/16架构（80%）上均得到复现，从而确立了“虚假标注关注头”是ViT系列架构在两个数据集和三种架构上的一致特性。全量微调并不能抑制这种行为，甚至可能使其固化：98.4%的虚假……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过机制可解释性方法首次在视觉Transformer中精确识别出一个专门读取X光片标注文字而非肺部病理的虚假注意力头（L8H10），经因果实验验证并跨两个数据集、三种架构复现，证明这是ViT家族的普遍特性，且全量微调无法消除、甚至可能加剧这种标注偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper mechanistically identifies a single spurious attention head (L8H10) in Vision Transformers that reads annotation text instead of lung pathology in chest X-rays, causally validates the bias via inpainting, replicates it across two datasets and three ViT-family architectures, and shows that full fine-tuning fails to suppress and may even entrench this annotation-driven bias.
